name: Anthropic
one_liner: Frontier AI lab behind the Claude models, sold mainly to enterprises and developers via API
story: Founded in 2021 by Dario and Daniela Amodei and other ex-OpenAI researchers around a safety-first pitch. Its 2022 Series B was led by Sam Bankman-Fried, whose FTX collapse months later left the stake in a bankruptcy estate, but Amazon and Google then committed billions in compute-linked investment. Claude's lead in coding and enterprise use took it from a $61.5B valuation in March 2025 to $380B in February 2026 and a reported $965B in May 2026 (AP), above OpenAI's last reported $852B.

name: xAI
one_liner: Elon Musk's AI lab behind Grok, merged with X and then acquired by SpaceX
story: Founded by Elon Musk in 2023, xAI built the Colossus supercomputer in Memphis in months and shipped Grok into X. It absorbed X in March 2025, raised at a $230B valuation in January 2026 while reportedly burning about $1B a month, and in February 2026 was folded into SpaceX in an all-stock deal valuing xAI at $250B. SpaceX then listed in June 2026 in a record $75B IPO at about $1.77T, so xAI's investors exited through Musk's rocket company rather than on xAI's own numbers.

name: Safe Superintelligence (SSI)
one_liner: Ilya Sutskever's lab building 'safe superintelligence' with no product before the goal is reached
story: Founded in June 2024 by OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy, SSI raised $1B at $5B within months and $2B at $32B in 2025 without releasing any model or product. Meta tried to buy it in 2025 and instead hired CEO Daniel Gross, leaving Sutskever as CEO. A reported Nvidia-led strategic investment of about $5B in July 2026 is unconfirmed by the company, and no product had shipped as of mid-2026.

name: Thinking Machines Lab
one_liner: Mira Murati's AI lab that raised a record $2B seed before shipping a product
story: Founded in February 2025 by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, it raised the largest seed round ever ($2B at $12B) and launched Tinker, a fine-tuning API. The founding team then scattered: co-founder Andrew Tulloch left for Meta in October 2025, CTO Barret Zoph and Luke Metz returned to OpenAI in January 2026, and Lilian Weng stepped down in July 2026. A planned round at up to $50B never closed; in November 2026 it was reported raising about $5B at a $40B pre-money valuation, with Nvidia supplying part.

name: Reka AI
one_liner: Multimodal model lab founded by ex-DeepMind and Google Brain researchers
story: Reka built multimodal models with a small team of former DeepMind and Google researchers. Talks for Snowflake to buy it for about $1B collapsed in 2024, and co-founder Yi Tay returned to Google. In July 2025 Nvidia and Snowflake led a $110M round that tripled its valuation to just over $1B, keeping it independent but far smaller than the frontier labs.

name: AI21 Labs
one_liner: Israeli LLM lab behind the Jurassic and Jamba models and the Wordtune writing app
story: Founded in 2017 by Yoav Shoham, Ori Goshen and Mobileye's Amnon Shashua, AI21 was an early GPT-3 rival and later shipped the Jamba hybrid Transformer/Mamba models. It reached $1.4B in 2023 but was squeezed by far larger labs. Calcalist reported in December 2025 that Nvidia was in advanced talks to buy it for $2-3B; the deal did not happen, and in 2026 it was reported in talks with Nebius.

name: Sakana AI
one_liner: Tokyo lab building nature-inspired, efficient AI models for Japan
story: Founded in 2023 by Transformer co-author Llion Jones and ex-Google researcher David Ha, Sakana skips brute-force scaling for techniques like evolutionary model merging and its 'AI Scientist'. Japanese banks and corporates backed it heavily, and a November 2025 Series B (reported as about $135M, while the company cited ¥32B) valued it at about $2.65B, making it Japan's most valuable unicorn.

name: Liquid AI
one_liner: MIT spinout building non-Transformer 'liquid' foundation models for efficient on-device AI
story: Spun out of MIT CSAIL in 2023 by Ramin Hasani, Mathias Lechner, Alexander Amini and Daniela Rus, Liquid AI builds 'liquid' foundation models based on dynamical-systems research rather than Transformers. AMD Ventures led a $250M Series A in December 2024 that valued it at over $2B (trackers range from $2.28B to $2.4B). Its LFM models target phones, cars and other edge devices where memory and power are tight.

name: Cartesia
one_liner: State-space-model lab from Stanford whose first product is ultra-low-latency voice AI
story: Founded by the Stanford researchers behind state-space models (including Albert Gu and Karan Goel), Cartesia bets on SSMs as a more efficient alternative to Transformers. It monetised first through Sonic, a fast text-to-speech model sold to voice-agent builders, and had raised about $191M by October 2025. No valuation has been disclosed.

name: Inception Labs
one_liner: Builds diffusion-based large language models (Mercury) that generate text in parallel
story: Founded by Stanford professor Stefano Ermon with Aditya Grover and Volodymyr Kuleshov, Inception applies the diffusion approach used in image models to text, so its Mercury models generate many tokens at once and run several times faster than autoregressive LLMs. It raised a $50M seed led by Menlo Ventures in November 2025; online claims of a $10B valuation are unsupported.

name: Essential AI
one_liner: Lab from two Transformer co-authors that pivoted from enterprise agents to open base models
story: Founded in 2023 by Ashish Vaswani and Niki Parmar, two authors of the Transformer paper, Essential raised a $56.5M Series A from investors including Google, Nvidia and AMD to build enterprise automation. Parmar left for Anthropic in late 2024 and the company pivoted to open research models, releasing the 8B-parameter open-weight Rnj-1 in December 2025.

name: Reflection AI
one_liner: Ex-DeepMind team pitching itself as America's open-weight frontier lab
story: Founded in 2024 by DeepMind's Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou to build coding agents, Reflection repositioned after DeepSeek as 'America's open frontier lab'. Its valuation went from $545M in March 2025 to $8B in October 2025 (Nvidia-led $2B) and roughly $25-27.5B in an April 2026 $2.5B round, before it had shipped a flagship model. It released its first open-weight model, Beam, in October 2026 and reportedly signed a ~$6.3B GPU deal with SpaceX's Memphis data centre.

name: Poolside
one_liner: Builds frontier models for software engineering, sold to enterprises and governments
story: Founded in 2023 by ex-GitHub CTO Jason Warner and Eiso Kant, Poolside trains its own models for coding using reinforcement learning from code execution and sells into enterprises and the public sector. After a $500M round at $3B in 2024 it planned a 2GW data-centre campus in Texas. In August 2026 Nvidia reportedly paid $6B for a non-exclusive licence to its 'model factory', hired 109 of its staff and invested $1B at a $12B pre-money valuation, a hybrid of investment and partial acqui-hire.

name: Aleph Alpha
one_liner: Germany's sovereign-LLM hope that quit the frontier race and was folded into Cohere
story: Founded by Jonas Andrulis in 2019, Aleph Alpha was pitched as Europe's answer to OpenAI and announced a '$500M' Series B in 2023 from Schwarz Group, Bosch and SAP, although much of it was reportedly grants and commitments rather than cash. By 2024 it had stopped trying to compete on frontier models and repositioned around its PhariaAI enterprise software. In April 2026 Cohere agreed to take it over with Schwarz Group as the key backer and both governments' blessing, closing later in 2026.

name: DeepSeek
one_liner: Quant-fund-backed Chinese lab whose cheap open-weight R1 model shook global markets
story: Spun out of the High-Flyer quant fund by Liang Wenfeng in 2023 and funded entirely by it, DeepSeek claimed a roughly $5.6M final training run for V3; its R1 reasoning model in January 2025 helped wipe about $589B off Nvidia's market value in a day. It shipped V4 in April 2026 and took its first outside money in June 2026, about $7.4B at a valuation above $50B, routed through a partnership controlled by Liang. A further ~$16B round and a STAR-market IPO were reported later in 2026 but are unconfirmed.

name: Moonshot AI
one_liner: Beijing lab behind the Kimi chatbot and the open-weight Kimi K2 models
story: Founded in 2023 by Yang Zhilin, Moonshot won early users with Kimi's long context window, then lost ground in China's 2024 chatbot ad war. Its open-weight Kimi K2 (July 2025) became a global favourite for agentic coding, and its valuation went from $4.3B at the end of 2025 to about $35B by July 2026 as annualised revenue reportedly reached $300M. A Hong Kong IPO is reported for 2027.

name: Zhipu AI (Z.ai)
one_liner: Tsinghua spinout behind the GLM models, the first of China's 'AI tigers' to go public
story: Spun out of Tsinghua University's knowledge-engineering lab in 2019, Zhipu sold its GLM models heavily to government and state-owned customers and was added to the US Entity List in January 2025. It listed in Hong Kong on 8 January 2026, raising about $558M and closing its debut at about HK$55.5B ($7.1B). By June 2026 the shares were up about 10x, a market value of about HK$580B (about $74B at 7.8 HKD/USD), overtaking MiniMax.

name: MiniMax
one_liner: Shanghai lab behind Hailuo video, the Talkie companion app and open-weight MiniMax models
story: Founded in 2021 by ex-SenseTime executive Yan Junjie, MiniMax earned unusually much from consumer apps abroad (Talkie) and its Hailuo video model. It listed in Hong Kong on 9 January 2026, a day after Zhipu, at a pre-listing value of more than HK$50B, and its shares jumped as much as 100% on debut. By June 2026 it traded at about HK$180B (about $23B) and had fallen behind Zhipu.

name: 01.AI
one_liner: Kai-Fu Lee's model lab that became a unicorn in eight months, then stopped training frontier models

near_death.what: Stopped pre-training frontier models; much of its pre-training team moved to an Alibaba Cloud lab and it repositioned as an enterprise deployment company

story: Founded by Kai-Fu Lee in 2023, 01.AI hit a $1B valuation within eight months with Alibaba's backing and released the Yi open models. Facing the cost of keeping up with larger rivals and DeepSeek's cheap models, in early 2025 it stopped chasing frontier pre-training, moved most of that team into a lab with Alibaba Cloud, and pivoted to selling customised enterprise deployments, often built on other companies' open models.

name: Krutrim
one_liner: Ola founder Bhavish Aggarwal's Indic AI lab, India's first AI unicorn, later shrunk to an AI cloud

near_death.what: Headcount fell from 550+ (Aug 2025) to about 150; consumer assistant Kruti pulled from app stores and a second layoff round cut almost half of remaining staff

story: Krutrim became India's first AI unicorn in January 2024 after a $50M round at $1B, promising Indic-language LLMs and an AI cloud. The models drew little use; Aggarwal pledged Ola Electric shares to raise debt for it, and by 2026 it had pulled its Kruti assistant, cut most of its staff and pivoted to AI cloud infrastructure.

name: Sarvam AI
one_liner: Bengaluru lab building Indian-language and sovereign foundation models
story: Founded in 2023 by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar, Sarvam was picked in April 2025 to build India's sovereign LLM under the IndiaAI Mission. Early open models drew criticism for low adoption, but in June 2026 it closed the first $234M of a $300M Series B at a $1.5B post-money valuation with Nvidia, Amazon and HCLTech, taking most of the money raised by Indian-language AI companies that year.

name: World Labs
one_liner: Fei-Fei Li's lab building 'world models' that generate explorable 3D worlds
story: Founded in 2024 by ImageNet creator Fei-Fei Li with Justin Johnson, Ben Mildenhall and Christoph Lassner, World Labs raised $230M at about $1B to build models that understand and generate 3D space. AMD, which already trained and served its models on AMD GPUs, agreed in September 2026 to buy it for about $8.2B in stock, with Li becoming AMD's chief scientist; the deal closed in November 2026.

near_death.what: Board fired CEO Sam Altman; most staff threatened to quit for Microsoft until he was reinstated five days later
